correctness.rationale: In the intrinsic edge-sum hyperplane the incidence identity BBᵀ=(n−2)I+11ᵀ gives the two stated orthogonal components. Coordinate normals have projected energies 2/n and (n−3)/(n−1), and subset normals have U-energy ||Bv−mean(Bv)1||²/(n−2); subtracting from ||v−mean(v)1||² gives the W-energy. Subset slacks are (s−1)(n−s)/n. For the round candidate the squared distances to these hyperplanes are minimized at s=2 or n−1 because their logarithmic derivative strictly decreases; the co-singleton endpoint is the smaller of the two. Its distance exceeds the coordinate radius exactly for integers n≥6 in scope. For n=4,5 the co-singleton cap binds together with the coordinate bound; substituting gives precisely the listed tangencies. The coordinate and subset inequalities in the stated contact list are genuine facets: the coordinate face is the base polytope for K_n with an edge deleted, which has connected cycle matroid for n≥4; a tight subset face factors into base polytopes of the restriction to K_s and the contraction, which has s parallel spokes for each remaining vertex plus its edges to the other remaining vertices. Both factors are matroid-connected (including the one-element restriction), so their dimensions add to m−2. Centered coordinate normals have zero sum and frame operator I; co-singleton normals are the negatives of centered incidence rows, with zero sum and frame operator (n−2)Π_U. After the shape transform and slack normalization, the listed weights give moments 0 and I, including the n=4 certificate using a subset of all contacts; this proves global, not merely symmetric, optimality. Volume follows from the multiplicities, and the n=3 regular triangle has squared inradius 1/6. An independently written rational check (`python3 -B /workspace/branches/bounded_review_checks.py 3`) evaluated actual labeled subset inequalities and matrix moments for n=4 through 10. Neither that finite check nor the supplied, inspected but unexecuted verifier is the all-order proof.
